summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic idiopathic pancreatitis was admitted for a moderate flare characterized by epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and low-grade fever. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, IV pain control including a Dilaudid PCA, and antiemetics. Due to slow improvement and moderate malnutrition, TPN was restarted and advanced to goal. Blood cultures, chest X-ray, and urinalysis showed no infection, and fevers resolved spontaneously. Her pain gradually improved to baseline, and she transitioned to oral hydromorphone while her fentanyl patch was reduced to 100 mcg/hr. She was advanced to a soft diet, managed for constipation, and continued on omeprazole twice daily for worsening GERD, with plans for outpatient EGD. She remained mentally clear, afebrile, and ambulatory, and was discharged home with TPN support, home health, and follow-up arranged.
